answer.generated: The relationship between requirements engineering and system design is inherently iterative and concurrent, with each phase influencing the other. Requirements are initially specified through structured analysis and design activities, but as design progresses, constraints from existing systems and emerging design choices may refine or add requirements. This interaction means that requirements are not static; they evolve as the design process unfolds, requiring continuous refinement and adaptation. Consequently, the specification of requirements becomes more precise and detailed as the system architecture takes shape, while new requirements may emerge from design decisions or discovered limitations.
